name: Alt: the UPLIFT L-desk on the left wall for the four screens, MITTZON job desk on the right, no guest bed
notes:
Alternative for Andrew's UPLIFT link (2026-10-24: "add standing desks for consideration for the office, this is large but try to accommodate something like this"), meeting F-62. The usable floor is the 106 x 106 square as in a: furniture from y 12 and upholstery from y 18 off the hatched heater wall (F-33, heater-depth-assumed), nothing below y 116 in front of the wardrobe or below y 122 in front of the door (F-31: the 36" landings, assumed-position:closet and assumed-position:door).
desk-l UPLIFT L-desk 80"Mx60"R, walnut laminate, electric sit/stand (22.6-50.9"): rot 270, the main along the left wall (x 0-30, y 36-116), the return at its south end (x 30-60, y 88.5-116), on the user's left as configured. The personal station: four 32" screens, three across the main on the HUANUO arms (the outer two angled in about 30 degrees, about 77") and the fourth on the return; three face across the window; the fourth, on the return, faces north, so when Andrew turns to it the window is directly behind him, 35" and 32" inside its ends on the line through his chair: turn that screen about 30° toward the right wall on its arm, so its reflection falls on that wall, or drop the blinds when it is bright (final audit 2026-10-26; the note said the opposite). F-38: it starts 36" below the window wall, so nothing stands in front of the window; F-31: its south end on the wardrobe's landing line (y 116); F-35: 44.5" from the main's front to the job desk · fits.
chair-1 FLINTAN: in the L's corner, x 31-59, y 52-80, facing the main; it swivels left to the return. chair-2 FLINTAN: the job desk's, x 46.5-74.5, y 22-50, 16" from the heater wall; the two chairs sit 2" apart in y, so both stations work at once · fits.
desk-1 MITTZON 47 1/4x31 1/2, electric sit/stand: right wall, rot 90, x 74.5-106, y 12-59.25, the separate job station: the laptop on the ELLOVEN beside one 32" monitor, with 3/4" to spare (47.25 − 28 − 18.5, F-62; a single arm for the monitor above the laptop would free 19", not in the catalog); F-33 6" from the heater face · fits. (Until the audit of 2026-10-25 it was the 55 1/8" MITTZON, which left 21" between its end and the L's return, the only way in from the door.)
storage-2 BESTÅ shelf unit with doors 47 1/4" (top): hung above the job desk on two suspension rails, underside about 73 1/2" up (the MITTZON rises to 49 5/8", 3 1/2" higher than c's TRAVSPORT, so the job monitor needs the extra height), its top about 88 1/2"; the ceiling is unmeasured (F-63, F-23; final audit 2026-10-26).
The way in from the door: up the right wall's lower half, 46" between the return's end and the wall, then into the room between the return's corner and the job desk's end, 32.6" (F-30); then the 44.5" aisle between the two desks. To reach the job desk you pass chair-1: about 15" with it pulled out, 30" with it tucked under the main.
lamp-1 TÅGARP: bottom-left corner, left of the wardrobe's landing. plant-1 FEJKA: top-left corner, left of the window and above the L's north end.
rug-1 LOHALS (rug): x 30-82, y 22-99, under both chairs (7.5" under the job desk's front: level its feet). rug-2 KOLON (rug): x 31-70.4, y 48-95.25, the chair mat under chair-1. rug-3 Anji Mountain bamboo chair mat 48 x 36" (rug): x 38-74, y 12-60, under chair-2 at the job desk, between the L's back and the job desk's front (final audit 2026-10-26: chair-2 rolled on the jute with the KOLON's edge under its casters).
lamp-2 RÖDFLIK (top): on the L's return. lamp-3 RÖDFLIK (top): on the job desk's front corner. art-1 PJÄTTERYD (top): right wall above the way in, y 80-102, one of the three canvases (a row of three needs 68" and the wall has 62.75"); the other two stack on the left wall's door end above the floor lamp, x 0, y 118-140.
No guest bed: opened, the chair bed would run into the L's return (at best 2.3" short whichever way the room is arranged), so this variant trades the guest bed for the L, as c does. No BESTÅ on the floor either: the only free wall is the way in from the door.
Kid safety (F-21): the job desk stands by the window and its chair rolls, so Maddie could climb to the window: fit window stops there (not in the catalog; the sill is unmeasured, F-38).
Audit 2026-10-25: the L moved 6" south and the job desk became the 47 1/4" MITTZON, opening the way in from 21" to 32.6" (F-30). Total $3,054.82, prices as of 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24 (those before today are price-stale, F-02).
Final audit 2026-10-26, for every office layout: the HUANUO arms are C-clamps on the desks' back edges, and every run desk stands flush against its wall, so either the desk stands off the wall by the clamp's depth (not on the listing: measure the arm; at 2" the way in past the L's return becomes 31.8" in e and g, still over 30") or the arms use their grommet mount (the UPLIFT is configured with two grommets). No outlets are mapped: three motors, five screens, a PC and the lamps need a power strip in each cable tray (the MITTZON page offers KOPPLA, not captured) with a slack loop for the desk's 25" of travel, on the left wall or the right wall above the door. The wardrobe's left door, open 90°, stands on its hinge line at x 10, 1/2" from the TÅGARP and 1 1/2" from the plant's pot: fit a 90° stop on that door, and measure the room door's width and the wardrobe's distance from the right corner (the door as drawn, opened flat, lands 2" over the wardrobe's end). The way from the door to the job desk and the window passes the parked chair at the run (or the L) with 13 to 18 1/2" to spare, so the 30" walkway holds with the chairs pushed in.
